entities.summary:
American Airlines Flight 11 was a pivotal event in modern world history that took place on September 11, 2001, at 8:46 a.m. in New York City, USA. This commercial airliner, hijacked by terrorists, tragically crashed into the North Tower of the World Trade Center, causing unprecedented destruction and loss of life. The 9/11 attacks were carried out by the Islamic extremist group al-Qaeda, led by Osama bin Laden, and resulted in the deaths of 2,753 people. The aftermath of the attacks led to a global war on terror, with far-reaching consequences for international relations, security, and the lives of people around the world.

The Flight 11 crash was one of four coordinated attacks that day, which also included the hijacking of United Airlines Flight 175, American Airlines Flight 77, and United Airlines Flight 93. The 9/11 attacks were the deadliest terrorist attack in history, and their impact can still be felt today.

The significance of the 9/11 attacks lies in their ability to change the course of global politics and international relations. The attacks led to a significant shift in US foreign policy, with a greater focus on counterterrorism and military intervention. The aftermath of the attacks also saw a significant increase in security measures around the world, including the creation of the Department of Homeland Security in the US.

In the years following the 9/11 attacks, there have been numerous memorials and tributes built to honor the victims. The National September 11 Memorial & Museum, located at the World Trade Center site, is a poignant reminder of the tragedy and its impact on the world.

The 9/11 attacks will always be remembered as a turning point in modern history, marking a new era of global politics and security measures.

The statistics are staggering: over 3,000 people died in the 9/11 attacks, and the economic impact was estimated to be over $3 trillion.
